newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life Finance optimistic about 1997.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life Finance optimistic about 1997.

text.p: Irish Life Finance Group (ILFG) on Thursday announced a multi-million pound investment affecting all areas of its business and said it was set to increase its market share over the next five years at the expense of traditional lenders.
Chief executive Brian MacManus said he was optimistic about the group's potential for growth during 1997 and expects lending of 250 million Irish pounds and mortgage lending of 150 million.
The company achieved gross lending of over 200 million Irish pounds last year.
MacManus was speaking at the opening of ILFG's new headquarters by Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn.

"We have already invested heavily in our new Dublin headquarters to accommodate a significant growth in our business and we are also in the process of opening new offices in Northern Ireland," MacManus said.
IFLG is also one year down the road on a group wide information technology project which will provide it with a fully-integrated platform to grow its business into the next millennium.

"The Irish economy is in great heart and we believe that we can continue to grow our retail business strongly in the residential and commercial lending markets," Paddy McEvoy, chairman of Irish Life Finance Group, said.
ILFG, which currently has an eight percent share of the residential lending market in Ireland, is a joint venture owned by Irish Life Plc and Irish Intercontinental Bank.
